newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile mulls privatizing copper firm Enami - report.
newsitem.headline: Chile mulls privatizing copper firm Enami - report.

text.p: A Chilean government commission is studying selling state copper company Enami's two smelters with interested buyers including local firm Pucobre and Phelps Dodge, said newspaper Estrategia Tuesday.
The Empresa Nacional de Minieria (Enami) operates two smelting-refining complexes and provides support to small mining companies.
None of the firms were immediately available for comment.

The government is considering selling Enami's Paipote smelter and the Ventanas smelting and refining complex to private investors, with the small mining companies' program remaining in state hands, said the paper.
Companies interested in Paipote, which lies in the northern Third Region, include Punta del Cobre (Pucobre) and Phelps Dodge which owns the nearby Candelaria copper mine.
Any decision to sell Enami could be announced in March, said the report which quoted unnamed mining sources.
Enami's commercial manager Sergio Taulis told Reuters last month that Enami has held early talks with companies including Minera Candelaria on smelter joint ventures.
Under its $150 million modernization program, Enami sees its output of refined copper output growing to 328,000 tonnes by 1999 from 214,000 tonnes this year.
Its smelted copper production should rise to 204,000 tonnes in 1999 from 190,000 tonnes this year.
